newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady, gas oil heads eastwards.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady, gas oil heads eastwards.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were broadly steady on Monday, despite crude's weakness.
Gas oil was firmer backed by local support and some players keen to bid prices up for Indian tender pricing purposes.

The arbitrage eastwards was still the main focus although opinion differed as to its strength. A Russian 28kt cargo was sold to a major at high fob +$3.75. Larger "arb friendly" cargoes were pegged around high fob quotes +$5.
Traders said 0.2 pct material was assessed at high fob quotes +$3.50-4, basis Italian islands, for large parcel against high fob +$2 for 20-25kt.
Diesel was well bid with one major prepared to pay May IPE +$12. A Ras Lanuf cargo was heard available in late April.
Gasoline was slightly firmer amid fairly tight supply although demand, at least out of countries such as Italy, Spain and France, remained lacklustre.
"I think a lot of users stocked up ahead of Easter and for the maintenance period. I'm not expecting to see too much demand until the second half of April," said an Italian trader.
Traders said there was some demand out of Libya and Turkey. State Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) said it wanted to import two gasoline cargoes to swap for crude.
Players said the product would most likely come from the Mediterranean.

Fuel oil prices held broadly steady in a slow start to the week, with most interest centred on Portugal's tender for two 25,000 tonne cargoes of high sulphur fuel, with the option for a third, which closed today.

Italian refiner ISAB was heard to have sold to a trader on Friday a 25,000 tonne high sulphur cargo for fob high quotes plus a premium, said to be between $1 and $1.50. Tunisia, Romania and Turkey were also heard needing high sulphur.
